answer: Each identity keeps a thread of signed round stamps, and the next stamp is sealed in copper whenever a payout is requested. A request against a thread with any gap fails at once: settlement stalls and the missing span must be re-proved from the last sealed pearl, stamp by stamp, before funds move. A fabricated identity therefore has to buy back every hole in its own history at 12,000 POA per repaired span, so each fake identity carries a re-proof bill of its own, while an honest record re-seals free.
